brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut: they keep 7.4% of every ₹100 they sell — well above the 5.0% of similar firms — so room exists in their price.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price reduction across rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.target: Target a 10–15% saving on current rates
priceAsk.basis: They keep 7.4% profit vs 5.0% at similar firms — a 2.4 percentage-point cushion. The market line shows induction-wad PP caps asking ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume — verdict is MARKET-FAIR with modest room to move. Their strong credit rating (CARE A+ / Stable) and healthy profit mean they can afford to sharpen their price.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (shift from 30 days to 15 days after receipt) in exchange for a 3–4% price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days earlier frees up ₹1.64 L of our cash. They borrow money at about 7.02%, so paying early saves them roughly that rate — trade it for a matching price cut.

brief.financialLeverage: PGP Glass is healthy: CARE A+ / Stable rating, ₹3373.51 Cr revenue, keeps 7.4% profit (vs 5.0% peer median), and generates ₹2899.48 Cr free cash. Their cash is stuck for 78 days (vs 71 days at peers) — a bit tighter than similar firms — and they carry two red flags: EPF payment delays and pending legal case(s). But we're tiny to them: our ₹39.99 L is just 0.01% of their sales. That means we must bundle volume, commit longer, or line up a credible second source (Manjushree, Mold-Tek) to get their attention. Push hard on price — they have the margin — but don't expect them to bend on payment terms unless we sweeten the deal.

evidence.point: They keep more profit than peers
Strong credit rating with no cooperation issues
We are a very small customer
Their cash is tied up slightly longer than peers
They have compliance and legal red flags
evidence.figure: EPF payment delays, Pending legal case(s)

evidence.point: Market reference for induction-wad PP caps shows room at volume

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate already on our books for packaging

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) — pails, containers, pharma bottles/closures; strong, profitable alternate already qualified for packaging

risks: We're 0.01% of their sales — on our own we have little pull; bundle more SKUs, commit 2–3 years, or bring Manjushree into the discussion to create competition.
EPF payment delays and pending legal cases are red flags — watch for disruption risk; qualify a second source (Manjushree or Mold-Tek) in parallel.
Their cash cycle is 78 days vs 71 days peer median — tighter than average — so if we push too hard on stretching payment terms without offering faster pay, they may walk.
Market backups (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are leads to qualify (verify capability and get quotes before using as leverage) — none are approved sources yet.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: You're a strong partner with a CARE A+ rating and healthy profit — 7.4% vs 5.0% at peers — so we'd like to talk about bringing your price in line with what the market and our other suppliers are showing, especially if we consolidate more volume with you.
